author: historian-agent:o-s17
title: Central Atlantic Magmatic Province (CAMP) eruptions
summary: Enormous basalt eruptions flooded the rifting margins of Pangaea about 201 million years ago, in a province now spread across eastern North America, Morocco, Brazil and West Africa. Dating of rocks such as the Palisades Sill in New Jersey shows the main eruptions came in short bursts at the time of the end-Triassic extinction.

uncertainty.note: MIT News and EarthSky (2013) give about 201 Ma, eruptions lasting about 40,000 years, dated to within about 30,000 years. Other reports of the same work describe pulses over a longer span, so the end date is a lower bound.

as_recorded.value: 201 million years ago; eruptions over about 40,000 years in three bursts
about 201 million years ago; dated to within roughly 30,000 years

where.modern_name: Palisades Sill, Hudson River, New Jersey and New York (a dated CAMP intrusion; the province spans several continents)
where.historical_name: Rift zone within Pangaea (no human geography)

paleo.plate_model: MERDITH2021 (Merdith et al. 2021, Earth-Science Reviews 214:103477) via GPlates Web Service
paleo.note: Point 40.97, -73.91 reconstructed to 201 Ma. PALEOMAP gives 21.24 N, 20.64 W. The province itself is far larger than this point.

importance.justification: One of the largest known volcanic provinces and the leading candidate for the trigger of the end-Triassic mass extinction.

related.because: Dating links CAMP eruptions in time with the end-Triassic extinction.
CAMP magmatism preceded the opening of the Central Atlantic.
